newsitem.title: MEXICO: Guatamala rebels slam kidnap by one of their own.
newsitem.headline: Guatamala rebels slam kidnap by one of their own.

text.p: Guatemala's leftist guerrillas on Wednesday condemned one of their former commmanders whose arrest for an alleged kidnapping has thrown the country's peace talks off track.

Earlier this month police arrested Rafael Augusto Valdizon Nunez, leader of one of four separate guerrilla groups that make up the URNG rebels, on suspicion of the kidnapping of an 86-year-old, wheelchair-bound woman.

The Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) said in a statement that it recognised that Valdizon, whom it called the "ex-commander Isaias," had taken part in the kidnapping and condemned his actions.
The URNG said the kidnapping of Olga Alvarado de Novella, wife of a weathy businessman, on Aug. 25 as she left church was done without the knowledge of the rebel group's command.

On Monday the government suspended peace talks planned for Tuesday in Mexico City, saying the recent abduction violated the terms of the peace process. The general command of the URNG is based in Mexico City.
The surprise government announcement came amid mounting anticipation that the government and the URNG would sign a final peace accord in December after 36 years of war.

On Wednesday the URNG washed its hands of the kidnappers, saying that it took "all political responsibility" for the crime but adding that none of the members of the rebel general command knew of the plan.

"The URNG is perfectly aware of the risk to the peace talks from this incident and is determined to do whatever is necessary so that they can continue and come to a peaceful conclusion," the rebel group said.
